property_summary: For any admissible input, reference P.transfer returns true; mutant M.transfer also returns true unconditionally, so there is no return-value difference. The real difference is that P executes external calls that may revert, so P.reverts if any call fails, while M never calls out and never reverts. Therefore, the general rule is: if P.transfer succeeds (does not revert), then all token transfers were actually performed (i.e., the external callee received at least one call). The buggy M succeeds without performing any transfers, so when an adversarial callee records whether it was called, the rule holds for P but fails for M.
change_summary: Delete the for loop body so no transfers are executed and return true is unconditional.
